To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed multimodal system achieves high person independent classification accuracies of up to 95% for discrimination of the relaxed state vs. workload.

the proposed system achieves high classification accuracy of 90% for person dependent and 94% for person independent classification of workload related biosignals, using short data frames (10 s) and that it is robust against changes in driving style, driving scenario, driving experience, age and gender of the driver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an online workload recognition system, which is capable of recognizing workload related biosignals in real-time.
the development of an online workload recognition system that can be used to support the driver in a realistic driving scenario.
the recognition of workload related changes in biosignals, and with the fusion of different biosignals for person independent workload recognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presented multimodal classification system is able to recognize the state of high workload reliably and with high sensitivity, but that the classification accuracy for relaxed states vs. low workload states could be improved by further investigations.
the presented approach provides a promising basis for the development of a person independent workload recognition system.

we have developed a robust system for online person independent recognition of mental workload, which is based on a large and representative training corpus, and which is capable of classifying workload states in real time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented multimodal classification system is able to detect workload related biosignal changes with high accuracy, even for persons not previously seen during training.
it is possible to classify workload related biosignals with high accuracy using a multimodal system that is independent of the person.
the presented system is capable of detecting the workload of a person, independent of the person, in real time, using only noninvasive biosignals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed system can be used as an online tool for monitoring the workload of an operator in a realistic environment.
the combination of the different modalities improves the classification performance.
it is possible to achieve person-independent classification results for workload using a small set of physiological signals.
